messages:
tara (eng-infra): Heads-up — seeing intermittent NVLink stalls on h100 nodes in us-west1 when running long batched generation jobs. Impact is tail latency spikes (~2-3s) and occasional kernel OOMs.

sam (dedicated-fleet): Investigating. Any correlation with driver or CUDA versions?

tara (eng-infra): Most affected nodes are on nvidia-driver 535 + CUDA 12.2. NCCL 2.18. Logs show repeated `nvlink timeout` and `gpu reset` events. Not seen on eu-west yet.

matt (SRE): ops-bot created alert: `dedicated.h100.us-west1.nvlink_stall` firing 3x in 10m. Can you paste a short log snippet?

ops-bot: ALERT: dedicated.h100.us-west1.nvlink_stall count=7 window=600s severity=high

lina (infra): Pasted minimal log from node h100-042: ```
[   12.345678] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[   12.346123] nvidia: GPU 0000:65:00: GPU lockup - switching to fallback
[   12.347000] nvlink: timeout waiting for peer response
```

sam (dedicated-fleet): Hmm. Those Xid=79s often point to driver/kernel mismatch or NIC firmware weirdness impacting PCIe/CCIX paths. Any recent NIC firmware pushes in us-west1?

lina (infra): We did a NIC FW push last week for bulk VPC offload (Mellanox FW 15.30). Only us-west1 H100 clusters upgraded so far.

nicole (runtime): Also saw a timing pattern: stalls start at ~1.5M tokens processed in a batch-run workload. Suggests a kernel interaction with continuous KV cache + large gather ops.

matt (SRE): For Dedicated we need a safe rollback plan. Current recommended steps: 1) Pause driver 535 rollouts to remaining regions. 2) Canary rollback to driver 530 on a small subset of affected nodes. 3) If rollback clears alerts for 30m, expand rollback. 4) Offer capacity shift to hosted pool for customer-critical routes.

sam (dedicated-fleet): Agree. Also propose phased drain: pick 6 nodes per AZ to roll back first, keep others serving. Draining policy: `kubectl cordon && drain --grace-period=120` with traffic routed to warm spare pool.

tara (eng-infra): Can we avoid mass reboots? Some customers on Dedicated can't tolerate interruption. We should prefer hot-replace where possible (detach GPU from hostd, reprovision). Riskier but less app impact.

lina (infra): Hot-replace path tested on a10s, not at scale on h100. Hardware team warning: NVLink resets may need host reboot to clear. Hot-swap might leave stale NCCL groups.

nicole (runtime): Short-term mitigation: enable `--nvlink-disabled-fallback` in runtime to avoid high-degree nvlink ops for large batches, and force model split across GPUs with `--split-shard=roundrobin`. This trades throughput for stability.

matt (SRE): We need immediate customer communication template. Sales + CSE should be told we may schedule targeted node reboots in next 4 hours for us-west1 Dedicated fleets. Ops: prepare maintenance notices and capacity shift playbook.

sam (dedicated-fleet): Action items: 
- sam: start selective rollback job to driver 530 on 6 nodes in us-west1-a (h100-042..047) now.
- lina: validate NIC FW rollback path and hold further FW pushes.
- nicole: deploy runtime flag to reduce nvlink degree on canary nodes.
- tara: coordinate with customer CSEs for impacted accounts and route them to hosted pool if needed.
- matt: monitor ops-bot alert thresholds and be ready to expand rollback.

tara (eng-infra): I'll notify product + support. Also request quota to spin up 50 hosted h100 minutes for overflow.

lina (infra): Starting nic rollback dry-run in staging. If OK, will trigger in prod canary after sam confirms driver job.

ops-bot: RUNBOOK NOTE: To rollback driver on Dedicated nodes: 
1) pin image `rwinf/dedicated-driver:530-compat`
2) drain node, run `install-driver 530`, restart nvidia modules, run `nvidia-smi -q` health check
3) run iterative `nccl-tests` and `latency-ppm` checks for 15m
4) uncordon if healthy

nicole (runtime): I'll push a canary config in `canaries/driver-compat` with `nvlink_degree: reduced`, runtime timeout bump, and a model-fallback policy to `server-hosted` when `nvlink_stall>=3`.

sam (dedicated-fleet): Driver rollback job kicked off to h100-042..047. ETA ~7m. Rolling one node at a time with health gate between nodes.

matt (SRE): If rollback doesn't reduce Xid rates in 30m, we escalate to full NIC FW rollback and open a vendor ticket with Mellanox/NVIDIA. Also consider temporary capacity caps to avoid long-run batches (cap batch_size to 4) to reduce risk.

tara (eng-infra): Noted. Keep updates here. If anyone needs to join voice: #incident-bridge up.

sam (dedicated-fleet): h100-042 driver 530 applied -> `nvidia-smi` shows no Xids. Running `nccl-tests --allreduce --size=16MB` loop.

lina (infra): Staging NIC rollback verified, planning prod schedule if canary looks good. Holding other regions.

matt (SRE): 20m since first canary node rollback, alerts have dropped to baseline. Good sign. Keep monitoring 1hr before wider expansion.

tara (eng-infra): Thanks all. Follow-up: postmortem draft and a proposal to improve canary policy for combined driver+FW pushes (separate windows, cross-check with runtime tests).

nicole (runtime): I'll add a synthetic workload that mimics long-batch KV cache stress to our canary suite.

ops-bot: INCIDENT STATE: mitigated -> monitoring.
